title: Plus One
statement: A non-negative integer is stored as an array of its decimal digits, most significant digit first, with no leading zeros (except the number 0 itself). Add one to the number and return the digits of the result as an array.

example.caption: The 9s turn to 0 and pass the carry left until the 2 takes it.

idea.sentence: Add one the way you do on paper: bump the last digit, and while a digit is 9 turn it to 0 and carry left, stopping at the first digit that can take the carry.

jargon.plain: The 1 you pass to the next digit on the left when a column adds up to 10.
The leftmost digit, the one worth the most. In [1,2,9] it is the 1.

watch.inputHint: One argument: an array of digits 0 to 9, like [1,2,9].

vars.meaning: number of digits in the array

compare.bruteLabel: Convert to a number, add, convert back
compare.optimalLabel: Carry digit by digit from the right

rows.name: Convert to a big number
rows.note: Join, parse, add, split. Breaks as soon as the number is longer than a normal integer holds, unless you have a big-integer type.

rows.name: Carry from the right
rows.note: Usually stops after one digit. Only a run of trailing 9s makes it walk further. The copy costs O(n) once.

fast.takeaway: Both are linear, but only the carry version works for any number of digits. The only thing that can go wrong is running past the left end.

stages.title: Start at the last digit
stages.note: Walk from the right end toward the left. The last digit is where the +1 lands.

stages.title: A 9 becomes 0
stages.note: 9 + 1 is 10. Write 0 here and carry the 1 to the digit on the left.

stages.title: The carry ends
stages.note: A digit below 9 absorbs it by going up one and we return. If the walk runs off the left end, every digit was 9, so return a new 1 followed by all the zeros.

edges.title: No carry
edges.why: The last digit is below 9, so it goes up and we return at once.

edges.title: A single 9
edges.why: The only digit turns to 0 and the carry has nowhere to go, so the array grows by one.

edges.title: Zero
edges.why: 0 is below 9, so it becomes 1. No special case is needed for the number zero.

edges.title: Carry stops before the front
edges.why: The 8 absorbs the carry. The result is the same length as the input, so do not add a leading 1 by habit.

gotchas.text: Return from inside the loop as soon as a digit below 9 absorbs the carry. If you keep looping, you add one to every remaining digit on the left.
Do not turn the digits into one integer. 20 nines overflow a 64-bit integer, and the array form exists exactly so you can avoid that.
Number('99999999999999999999') loses digits, because a JS number is a 64-bit float with only about 15 safe digits. Stay with digit arrays or BigInt.
A new leading digit costs an unshift or a spread. After the loop, every element is already 0, so [1, ...out] gives the right answer without a second pass.
append([]int{1}, out...) builds the longer slice. Do not append to the input digits slice: if it has spare capacity, the caller's backing array changes. The code here copies first.

recap.key: Walk right to left. A 9 becomes 0 and carries. The first digit below 9 takes +1 and ends it. If none does, prepend 1.
recap.complexity: Time O(n). Space O(n) for the copy, O(1) extra.
moves: If digit < 9: add one and return
Else set it to 0 and move left
Ran off the left end: return [1] followed by the zeros
